The FOMC statement is cautiously optimistic—labor market solid, growth moderate, a 25 bp hike to 0.75–1.00% with continued reinvestments to keep policy accommodative. Incorporating SLOOS tilts the tone a bit more measured: banks report/expect tighter standards in CRE (including foreign banks) and foresee deteriorating asset quality in autos and credit cards, while C&I standards are largely unchanged with some expected easing and mortgage standards mostly little changed or easing (notably for GSE-eligible and some jumbo segments). Foreign banks also report weaker business loan demand and plan tighter C&I/CRE standards. These mixed-to-slightly-tightening credit signals imply headwinds in certain sectors, reinforcing the Fed’s gradualism rather than a hawkish shift. Adjusting for SLOOS, the sentiment is positive but modestly tempered.
